definition: Pedal steel guitar is prominent in the arrangements.
Fiddle or violin plays a lead or featured role.
Bottleneck or lap-steel slide guitar is a signature texture.
Programmed drums are a defining texture.
Fingerstyle acoustic guitar is the core of the sound.
Loose, thick, distorted electric guitar in the Neil Young & Crazy Horse mold.
Twin or triple lead guitars in harmony (Allmans, Skynyrd, Thin Lizzy line).
Bright, ringing, chiming clean electric guitar.
Massed distortion and feedback used as texture.
Bright, snappy country lead guitar (Bakersfield and honky-tonk style).
Southern or rural accent shapes the singing.
Tight vocal harmonies (Everly/Louvin style or band harmonies).
Jokes and grief in the same verse (Prine/Berman line).
Dark, grotesque, or religious Southern imagery.
Named brands, athletes, TV, and pop ephemera.
Breakups and lost love as the main subject.
Bars, hangovers, and drinking as setting or subject.
Religious or gospel themes and forms.
Home-recorded, tape hiss, deliberately rough sound.
Full-band live-to-tape feel with little overdubbing.
At least one song over seven minutes.
